nodes.description:
Pathogenic variants in RNU4ATAC (2q14.2) are single-nucleotide substitutions in a non-protein-coding snRNA gene, clustering in two structurally critical regions of U4atac — the 5' stem-loop (n.30G>A, n.50G>A/C, n.51G>A, n.55G>A; n.51G>A is an Old Order Amish founder allele) and the Stem II domain (n.16G>A, n.111G>A, n.124G>A). Most act by disrupting the snRNA's secondary structure and its binding of essential di-snRNP protein components; n.124G>A acts differently, by reducing U4atac abundance. Complete loss of U4atac is expected to be lethal, so disease alleles are hypomorphic rather than null.
A 2026 reevaluation of every published RNU4ATAC case makes the genotype-phenotype relationship explicit and gives it a structural basis: genotypes in which the variants are located *exclusively* in the 5' stem-loop produce the severe, lethal MOPD I end of the spectrum, while a genotype carrying at least one variant that spares the 5' stem-loop gives a milder phenotype with later onset - Roifman or Lowry-Wood syndrome. The reason is that the 5' stem-loop is where U4atac binds the essential di-snRNP proteins NHP2L1 and PRPF31, so sparing it preserves partial function. This is the single most useful predictive rule in the RNU4ATAC-opathies, and it is why the three disorders are separate dismech entries rather than subtypes of one.

nodes.description: The functional consequence is selective mis-splicing of U12-type (minor) introns, present in roughly 700 human genes, while U2-dependent (major) intron splicing is unaffected. The defect is selective at the level of splicing rather than expression: transcriptomic analysis of TALS patient-derived cells shows distinct U12-type intron splicing profiles versus controls but largely unchanged mRNA levels. The specificity of the lesion is demonstrated by rescue — introducing wild-type U4atac into MOPD I cells restores U12-dependent splicing.

nodes.description:
The retinal arm of the RNU4ATAC-associated pigmentary triad: deficient or absent retinal pigmentation, reported alongside the hair and skin findings in the same patients. This is distinct from the Retinal Dystrophy entry below, which is a degenerative claim drawn from the broader RNU4ATAC spectrum; this is a developmental pigmentary deficit described in MOPD I specifically. HP:0007894 is defined as reduced fundus pigmentation evaluated in the context of skin and hair color, which is exactly how both sources report it.
frequency is intentionally omitted for the same reason as the hair and skin arms.

nodes.description:
Pigmentary abnormality of the hair — yellowish-gray hair and an unusually fair complexion — has been reported in RNU4ATAC-confirmed MOPD I, with skin biopsy showing abnormal melanin function despite normal oculocutaneous albinism genes. Note that this is a pigmentary rather than a structural hair abnormality; see the entry notes on why sparse/absent hair is not curated here. The skin and fundus arms of the same finding are curated separately below, because HP:0011358 is hair-specific by definition.
frequency is intentionally omitted: the only denominators available are two small series from a single group, and the disease-level rate is unknown. See the entry notes.

nodes.description: Because minor introns are concentrated in genes governing DNA replication and repair, transcription, RNA processing, and translation, minor splicing failure compromises the cell populations most dependent on those processes during embryogenesis — cortical neural progenitors and growth plate chondrocytes above all. The result is the combined brain-and-bone phenotype: severe microcephaly with structural cortical malformation and a generalized skeletal dysplasia, on a background of extreme prenatal growth restriction.

nodes.description: Destabilized U4atac reduces formation of the U4atac/U6atac.U5 tri-snRNP, the catalytic core of the minor spliceosome. Patient fibroblasts and iPS cells homozygous for the common n.51G>A allele show reduced tri-snRNP levels, and the resulting splicing defect is a direct consequence of that assembly failure rather than of reduced snRNA transcription.

nodes.description: Minor-intron-containing genes are significantly enriched for cilium assembly functions, so minor splicing failure secondarily impairs primary cilium biogenesis. This is supported by altered cilium function in patient fibroblasts and by a u4atac zebrafish model with ciliopathy-related phenotypes rescued by wild-type but not variant human U4atac, and it explains why some individuals with biallelic RNU4ATAC variants present with Joubert-syndrome-like features. This is a secondary (downstream) arm, not the primary lesion.
